task: Three facade skins redrawn for native Farmyard Commando wall and doorway proportions
notes: New sibling v3 PNGs; previous approved images retained unchanged.
Wall strips contain five bays in a fixed 5x2m appearance repeat, matching five unchanged 1x2m wall modules.
Ground-floor entrances use fixed 3x2m art regions on native piers/lintel; actual mask bounds are measured and mapped to the unchanged 1x1.65m opening.
Generative image mask placement is approximate; no pixel resizing, cropping or post-generation editing is performed.
Additional stories compose source wall modules at 2.12m floor spacing; no wall, door, actor, rig, pivot, source UV or collision change.
Nautilus contribution candidate; no Nautilus importer, engine manifest schema or consumer integration is claimed.

assets.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: ONE opaque horizontally repeating diffuse/albedo texture for the shared Nautilus game-asset library, authored directly for the unchanged Farmyard Commando wall geometry.
Input image 1 is a historical form reference. Input image 2 is the accepted painted style/palette reference. Neither is an edit target.
TECHNICAL PROPORTIONS: create a flat frontal orthographic 5:2 rectangle representing exactly FIVE METRES wide by TWO METRES high. Exactly FIVE identical narrow bays, each ONE METRE wide; centers at 10%,30%,50%,70%,90% of canvas width. A bay is twice as tall as wide. The original wall mesh is one metre wide, two metres high, 0.16 metre thick. Build the painting to fit that, preserving tall slender windows. Do not compress three broad windows into this strip. Continuous level top entablature and bottom plinth; half of an identical divider at left/right crop edges so copies join. Identical neutral edge colors and continuous trim heights, no exterior border. Pattern must repeat horizontally.
SUBJECT: Manufactures and Liberal Arts Building, Chicago 1893. Five slender round-headed glazed bays, slim Corinthian dividers, small circular medallions in the spandrels, a narrow geometric quatrefoil frieze and dentil cornice in the top 12% of wall. Subdued blue-grey closed glazing with delicate vertical mullions. Warm ivory staff and pale limestone relief. Each window sits above a short closed balustrade/sill in the bottom 18%.
Warm carved plaster in the accepted hand-painted game aesthetic: shallow readable relief, economical ornament, restrained weathering and subtle brush texture. Even diffuse illumination; no perspective, directional cast shadows, scenery, sky, people, vegetation, lettering, numbers, labels, border or watermark. No doorway, entrance, roof or whole building. Full-bleed opaque rectangular wall, all recesses sealed. Historical monochrome source informs facade vocabulary; color is an art choice.

Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: ONE opaque game diffuse/albedo entrance panel, authored directly for the unchanged native Farmyard Commando wall/door proportions, for the shared Nautilus art library.
Image 1 is the original 1893 building photograph, a form reference. Image 2 is our accepted painted wall strip, a style/palette reference. Neither is an edit target.
GEOMETRY IS FIXED: create a LANDSCAPE 3:2 full-bleed rectangle representing exactly 3 metres wide by 2 metres high, assembled from THREE 1m wall tiles. The middle tile has a rectangular 1m wide by 1.65m high opening, leaving ONLY 0.35m of lintel above. Left and right piers are each exactly 1m wide and 2m high. This is a compact SINGLE STORY human-scale entrance, not a monumental portal.
THE MASK: reserve one plain flat dark-blue-grey RECTANGLE, exactly from x=33.333% to66.667% of canvas width, extending from the bottom edge up to82.5% of total height (its top is17.5% below canvas top). Straight vertical sides, straight horizontal top, no sill, no threshold, no steps, no arch cutting into the mask, no extra openings. Actual geometry removes this dark rectangle, so keep every capital, molding and ornament OUTSIDE it. The remaining shallow lintel band above is only17.5% of canvas height. There must be no dark recess above the opening that suggests another taller door.
BUILDING: Manufactures and Liberal Arts, Chicago1893. Compact entrance with slender fluted Corinthian pilasters on the two full-width side piers, small round medallions at their tops and delicate geometric/quatrefoil banding. Within the shallow lintel, a low coffered arch MOTIF drawn in ivory relief above the rectangular door and fine dentils. No giant attic or tall closed lunette. Pale limestone ivory and subdued blue-grey mask, match Liberal Arts reference.
Keep the ornament inside the rectangular wall panel. Match the accepted hand-painted carved plaster, warm ivory subtle shallow relief, simplified game-readable details and very restrained weathering. Flat front orthographic albedo, uniform diffuse light, no perspective, deep projecting porch, directional cast shadows, sky, roof, scenery, people, flags, text, dates, numbers, border or watermark. Full-bleed opaque image. Original wall proportions take priority over monumental historical proportions; adapt the ornament rather than shrinking the door in a giant facade.
